_meta.title: 100-app agent-toolkit buildability research — final dataset
_meta.pipeline: pass1 (parametric baseline) -> pass2 (primary-doc retrieval) -> pass3 (multi-source + automated MCP liveness/content probe + human adjudication)

field_definitions.auth: Credential type a developer actually uses against the public API.
field_definitions.access: self_serve_free = credentials obtainable on a free plan/free trial/free dev account with no human in the loop; self_serve_paid = obtainable without approval but only on a paid plan; gated = requires admin/app review/existing customer contract; partner = requires partnership or contact-sales negotiation.
field_definitions.breadth: narrow (<~15 endpoints/one job) | medium | broad (full platform CRUD)
field_definitions.mcp: official = vendor-published and verified live; community = third-party only; none = none found
field_definitions.verdict: build = a Composio toolkit could ship today on a self-serve credential; caveats = buildable but access friction (approval, paid tier, customer-only); blocked = no viable public path today
field_definitions.confidence: high = 2+ independent sources or vendor doc quote; medium = single vendor doc/search synthesis; low = weak or indirect evidence

records.one_liner: Enterprise CRM and application platform.
records.blocker: None for development — free Developer Edition org; production data lives in a customer org.
records.note: Docs quote: 'OAuth authorization flows grant a client app restricted access to REST API resources.' Also SOAP + Bulk + GraphQL surfaces.

records.one_liner: CRM, marketing and sales automation suite.
records.blocker: None. Free CRM tier plus free developer test accounts.
records.note: Docs mention the 'remote HubSpot MCP server' directly in auth docs.

records.one_liner: Sales-pipeline CRM for SMB sales teams.
records.blocker: No free tier — API token requires a paid seat or an active trial.
records.note: 'API token' via x-api-token header, or OAuth 2.0 for marketplace apps. No vendor MCP doc resolved (404 on two candidate paths).

records.one_liner: Modern, data-model-flexible CRM.
records.blocker: None. MCP and API included on the free plan.
records.note: Official remote MCP at mcp.attio.com/mcp, OAuth login, available on all plans including Free.

records.one_liner: Open-source CRM (AGPL), cloud or self-hosted.
records.blocker: None. Self-host gives unlimited free credentials.
records.note: 'REST and GraphQL' both supported: Core API (CRUD) + Metadata API (schema). Bearer API key.

records.one_liner: Citrix work-management / lightweight CRM platform.
records.blocker: Product is in maintenance mode — Citrix states it does not maintain the API client libraries and tells customers to fork them.
records.note: 'Four different ways of authenticating' — server-side, client-side, username/password, app authentication.

records.one_liner: CRM inside the wider Zoho business suite.
records.blocker: None. Free edition and free developer console.
records.note: OAuth 2.0 only. Zoho ships four prebuilt CRM MCP servers (Data Insights, Data Ops, Module Customization, Workflow).

records.one_liner: Inside-sales CRM with built-in calling and email.
records.blocker: No free tier; trial only.
records.note: API keys over HTTP Basic. Vendor MCP docs live and MCP-dense.

records.one_liner: CRM built around Google Workspace.
records.blocker: Paid plan required; OAuth2 is positioned for partners.
records.note: 'Two ways to access the Copper Developer API: API keys and OAuth2.0' — key + account email in headers.

records.one_liner: Intapp's CRM/deal platform for private capital and advisory.
records.blocker: Credentials are issued inside a licensed customer tenant — no self-serve signup, no sandbox.
records.note: Docs announce a 'DealCloud MCP Server — client preview starting July 2026'. Vendor-published but customer-gated.

records.one_liner: Ticketing and customer-service platform.
records.blocker: None to develop (free trial); API tokens are being deprecated in favour of OAuth.
records.note: MCP is per-tenant (https://<subdomain>.zendesk.com/api/mcp) and still rolling out — announced at Relate 2026, no public setup docs at time of research. Flagged as the shakiest MCP call in the set.

records.one_liner: Customer messaging, helpdesk and Fin AI agent.
records.blocker: Paid workspace for production data; free developer workspaces exist for building.
records.note: Access Token for own workspace, OAuth for public apps. MCP docs offer one-click Cursor/VS Code install.

records.one_liner: Freshworks helpdesk and ticketing.
records.blocker: None — trial issues a key immediately; rate limits scale with plan.
records.note: 'curl -v -u apikey:X' — personal API key as basic-auth username. Rate limits documented per plan (Blossom/Garden 3,000/hr, Estate/Forest 5,000/hr).

records.one_liner: Shared inbox and customer-communication hub.
records.blocker: Paid plan; OAuth recommended for public integrations.
records.note: Auth docs list an explicit 'MCP server' scope: 'connect Front data exposed via MCP server to clients like Claude, ChatGPT'.

records.one_liner: B2B support platform built on shared Slack/Teams channels.
records.blocker: 'Only Admin users can create API tokens' and pricing is sales-led — no free self-serve developer path.
records.note: Doc URL guessing failed twice here (two 404s) before the working path was found — a documented agent failure mode. Correction from the probe: the 404 page still carried 16 MCP mentions, which led to the real doc — Pylon ships an official remote MCP at mcp.usepylon.com (OAuth, enabled in Settings > AI Controls).

records.one_liner: Multichannel helpdesk with live chat and call centre.
records.blocker: API reference is served per-tenant at https://YOURDOMAIN.ladesk.com/docs/api/v3/ — there is no public docs URL to crawl, and keys are admin-created.
records.note: 'apikey' header; 180 requests/minute per key.

records.one_liner: Developer-first support tool for B2B SaaS.
records.blocker: None technically — GraphQL API is at full parity with the UI.
records.note: Docs: 'no limitations in what can be done via the API vs the UI' and 'If you're looking to access our GraphQL API from an Agent, try our MCP Server instead.'

records.one_liner: Simple shared-inbox helpdesk for small teams.
records.blocker: Paid plan; OAuth only (authorization code + client credentials).
records.note: No OAuth-free static token path — client credentials flow is the machine-to-machine option.

records.one_liner: Helpdesk purpose-built for ecommerce stores.
records.blocker: Paid store plan required.
records.note: 'Private app → API key' / 'Public app → OAuth2'.

records.one_liner: People-centred customer service platform for enterprise.
records.blocker: Enterprise contract; an admin must grant the 'API User' permission before a token can be generated.
records.note: Token-based Basic auth pairing agent email + API token, per-org host https://{org}.gladly.com/api/v1/.

records.one_liner: Team chat and workflow platform.
records.blocker: Free to build; managed workspaces can require admin approval to install the app.
records.note: Slack-hosted remote MCP at mcp.slack.com/mcp, OAuth-based, announced 17 Feb 2026; admins approve client connections.

records.one_liner: Programmable SMS, voice and messaging APIs.
records.blocker: None — trial account issues credentials instantly; sending costs money.
records.note: Account SID + auth token (HTTP Basic) or scoped API keys. Vendor MCP docs live and MCP-dense.

records.one_liner: Zoho's team chat product.
records.blocker: None. Free plan plus free Zoho developer console.
records.note: 'OAuth 2.0' only: 'Clients are not required to support password authentication or store user credentials.'

records.one_liner: ByteDance's chat + docs + calendar suite (Feishu internationally).
records.blocker: App creation is self-serve, but a tenant admin must review and approve each app version before it works in production.
records.note: app_id/app_secret exchanged for tenant_access_token / user_access_token — not standard OAuth2. Docs are partly Chinese-only, which slowed the agent down.

records.one_liner: Budget team-chat app from CAKE.com (Clockify family).
records.blocker: None — API keys are generated with a /api-keys slash command and the feature is available on all plans.
records.note: Swagger-documented REST plus an official Node SDK with an OAuth2Client.

records.one_liner: Community chat platform with a large bot ecosystem.
records.blocker: Free; bots crossing 100 servers need verification.
records.note: OAuth2 for user-context, bot tokens for bot routes: 'bot users have full access to most API routes without using bearer tokens.'

records.one_liner: Messaging app with a first-class Bot API.
records.blocker: None — @BotFather issues a token in seconds, free.
records.note: 'Each bot is given a unique authentication token when it is created.' Bot API is HTTP/JSON; user-account access (MTProto) is a separate, harder surface.

records.one_liner: Meta's business messaging channel (Cloud API).
records.blocker: Meta app + WhatsApp Business Account + phone number provisioning; business verification and paid per-conversation messaging for real volume.
records.note: Temporary tokens for testing; production uses system-user tokens with whatsapp_business_messaging / _management permissions.

records.one_liner: Cloud phone system for sales and support teams.
records.blocker: Paid seat, and only Admin/Owner roles can see the Integrations & API section.
records.note: HTTP Basic with api_id as username and api_token as password; OAuth for public integrations.

records.one_liner: CPaaS for SMS, voice, video and verification.
records.blocker: None — free trial credit; JWT signing needed for the application-based APIs.
records.note: 'API Key and Secret (Header)' Basic auth for some products, JWTs for others — a per-product auth split that a toolkit has to model. Probe confirmed a vendor MCP page at developer.vonage.com/en/mcp.

records.one_liner: Google's search and display advertising platform.
records.blocker: A developer token must be approved by Google. Test-account access is immediate; Basic access (real accounts) requires review, Standard access requires more.
records.note: REST + gRPC. Docs list a 'Google Ads MCP server' in the developer toolkit. Brand verification (pilot since 7 Jul 2026) can cut review to hours.

records.one_liner: Facebook/Instagram advertising APIs.
records.blocker: App Review for ads_management plus business verification and an active ad account before production access.
records.note: Graph API, versioned. The gating is the whole story here, not the API surface.

records.one_liner: LinkedIn campaign management and marketing APIs.
records.blocker: Marketing Developer Platform access is a case-by-case application reviewed by LinkedIn, often weeks. Only 'Open Permissions' work without approval, and the 2-legged client-credentials flow is explicitly unavailable for marketing use cases.
records.note: Sales Navigator (SNAP) partner applications were closed to new applicants as of 2026. The clearest 'needs outreach, not engineering' row in the set.

records.one_liner: White-label marketing/CRM platform for agencies.
records.blocker: A paid GHL subscription; marketplace apps need approval to be listed publicly, private ones do not.
records.note: Private Integration Tokens are effectively static OAuth2 access tokens generated in account settings — the fastest path for a toolkit.

records.one_liner: Email marketing and audience management.
records.blocker: Free plan works; some endpoints depend on plan level.
records.note: 'API keys and OAuth 2 tokens can be used to make authenticated requests the same way.' Docs note access depends on 'what level of Mailchimp plan you have'.

records.one_liner: Ecommerce marketing automation (email/SMS).
records.blocker: None — private key on the free plan; OAuth apps need review only to be listed in the marketplace.
records.note: Three auth modes: private key (server-side), OAuth (apps), public key (client-side).

records.one_liner: All-in-one funnel builder, email and course platform.
records.blocker: None for core endpoints — the API is available on the free plan (up to 3 keys per account).
records.note: Baseline pass guessed 'paid only' — retrieval corrected it to free-plan available.

records.one_liner: Visual discovery platform with content and ads APIs.
records.blocker: Two-step review: Trial access after app review (capped at 1,000 requests/day), Standard access requires submitting a video of the app using the OAuth flow.
records.note: The trial cap is low enough that any real toolkit needs the Standard upgrade.

records.one_liner: Meta's text-based social network.
records.blocker: App Review required for anything beyond tester accounts; the 'Threads use case' must be chosen at app creation.
records.note: Short-lived (1h) or long-lived (60d, refreshable) Threads user access tokens. Surface is narrow: posts, replies, insights.

records.one_liner: Twilio's transactional and marketing email API.
records.blocker: None — free tier and instant API key; sender verification needed to actually send.
records.note: Bearer API key: 'Use another method of authentication separate from your account username and password.'

records.one_liner: Hosted ecommerce platform and app ecosystem.
records.blocker: None — free Partner account and unlimited development stores; public apps need review to be listed.
records.note: GraphQL Admin API is the supported surface (REST Admin is legacy). Custom apps use a static Admin API access token.

records.one_liner: WordPress ecommerce plugin.
records.blocker: None — self-hosted, keys generated in wp-admin. Each merchant is a different host, which is the real integration cost.
records.note: Consumer key/secret via HTTP Basic over HTTPS, or OAuth 1.0a one-legged over HTTP.

records.one_liner: SaaS ecommerce platform for mid-market retail.
records.blocker: None — free sandbox/dev store; store API accounts issue tokens directly.
records.note: REST for admin plus GraphQL Storefront API. BigCommerce ships a Storefront MCP aimed at shopper-facing agents rather than a full admin MCP.

records.one_liner: Salesforce B2C Commerce (Demandware) storefront platform.
records.blocker: Requires a licensed B2C Commerce instance and Account Manager access — no free sandbox for outsiders; partner programme in practice.
records.note: 'Shopper APIs are secured with the Shopper Login and API Access Service (SLAS), but SCAPI Admin APIs are secured with Account Manager instead' — two different auth systems in one product.

records.one_liner: Adobe's enterprise ecommerce platform; Magento Open Source is free.
records.blocker: Open Source edition is self-hostable for free; Adobe Commerce (PaaS) is licensed. Integration tokens are created in admin.
records.note: Auth page is scoped: 'This topic is for Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) customers only.' Token, OAuth 1.0a integration, and session auth all exist.

records.one_liner: Website builder with a commerce layer.
records.blocker: API keys require a commerce-capable plan (Core/Plus/Advanced/Commerce Advanced); OAuth requires becoming an approved Squarespace developer partner.
records.note: Orders/Inventory/Transactions APIs are individually plan-gated.

records.one_liner: Lightspeed's embeddable store widget for existing sites.
records.blocker: 'Only stores on paid plans can access API' (Venture, Business, Unlimited).
records.note: Custom apps get non-expiring secret + public tokens, skipping the OAuth dance. No vendor MCP found — only third-party wrappers (Zapier, Pipedream, Vinkius).

records.one_liner: Creator storefront for digital products.
records.blocker: None — free account, token generated in settings for personal use.
records.note: OAuth2 apps at gumroad.com/oauth/applications; API surface is small (products, sales, subscribers).

records.one_liner: Amazon marketplace seller/vendor APIs (SP-API).
records.blocker: Professional (not Individual) Seller account, developer registration with identity verification, and Appstore approval for public apps. Private apps are self-authorized.
records.note: Login with Amazon (LWA) OAuth; restricted data (PII) needs Restricted Data Tokens and role approval.

records.one_liner: Creator sales/payments platform — rebranded to Commas on 14 July 2026.
records.blocker: Requires a seller account; the docs live at apidocs.fan, not on the marketing domain.
records.note: The agent's first pass declared 'no public API'. fanbasis.com 301s to commas.com, and the API reference (checkout sessions, webhooks, customers, subscriptions, discount codes) sits on a third domain. Retrieval caught a rebrand the model's weights did not have.

records.one_liner: Wholesale SERP, keyword and backlink data APIs.
records.blocker: Prepaid balance required; no meaningful free tier.
records.note: HTTP Basic with base64 login:password. Official MCP covers 10 API modules; remote endpoint at mcp.dataforseo.com/mcp.

records.one_liner: SEO platform: rank tracking, audits, competitor data.
records.blocker: Paid plan or the $50 pay-as-you-go API package.
records.note: API included with subscription plans; vendor ships an MCP server for Claude/Cursor/Codex.

records.one_liner: Backlink and SEO intelligence suite.
records.blocker: API v3 is included from the Lite plan ($129/mo) upward and metered in API units — expensive, and unit budgets cap agent usage.
records.note: Lite 100k units / Standard 400k / Advanced 1M / Enterprise 2M. Could not confirm a vendor MCP server from primary sources — left as 'none' deliberately. Probe confirmed a vendor MCP page (55 MCP mentions) at ahrefs.com/mcp; the paid-units gating still applies to it.

records.one_liner: No-code/AI scraping service with agent-style scrapers.
records.blocker: Token-metered freemium; sign-up is instant.
records.note: Docs advertise an 'MCP Server' for AI agents alongside the REST scraper API.

records.one_liner: Marketplace and runtime for web-scraping actors.
records.blocker: None — free monthly credits, token on the Integrations page.
records.note: Bearer token; OpenAPI schema published. Remote MCP at mcp.apify.com exposes the actor catalogue as tools — arguably the closest thing to a competitor-shaped surface in this set.

records.one_liner: Web crawling and page-to-markdown API for LLM pipelines.
records.blocker: None — free credits on signup.
records.note: Five endpoints: scrape, crawl, map, search, extract. Bearer 'fc-' keys.

records.one_liner: Proxy network plus scraping/unlocker APIs.
records.blocker: Paid usage and KYC for residential-network products.
records.note: 'API Access' via API key or 'Native Access' with proxy username/password — billed identically.

records.one_liner: Open-source CLI that hunts usernames across 400+ sites.
records.blocker: Not an API at all — MIT-licensed CLI. A toolkit means hosting and wrapping the binary, and inheriting its rate-limit/blocking behaviour.
records.note: 'pipx install sherlock-project'. No auth, no hosted service, no vendor. The category's odd one out.

records.one_liner: Waterfall B2B contact/company enrichment across 30+ vendors.
records.blocker: Credit-based paid usage and a sales-led motion, though a key is issued on signup.
records.note: x-api-key header. Endpoints: prospector, contact/phone/company enrichment, email verifier.

records.one_liner: GTM data orchestration and enrichment workspace.
records.blocker: The public API (launched July 2026, all plans, clay-api-key header) has no versioned endpoint catalogue, no public base URL and no OpenAPI spec; the richer People & Company API is Enterprise-only and undocumented.
records.note: Two-tier reality: a thin documented public API plus an undocumented enterprise one. Good example of 'has an API' being the wrong question.

records.one_liner: Code hosting, CI and collaboration platform.
records.blocker: None.
records.note: Fine-grained/classic PATs, GitHub App installation tokens, OAuth apps, GITHUB_TOKEN in Actions. REST + GraphQL.

records.one_liner: Frontend hosting and serverless platform.
records.blocker: None — free hobby tier, bearer tokens in account settings.
records.note: Large documented REST surface (deployments, projects, domains, access groups, env vars).

records.one_liner: Web hosting and edge platform.
records.blocker: None — free PATs with configurable expiry.
records.note: OpenAPI-based REST at api.netlify.com/api/v1; 500 req/min general, 3 deploys/min.

records.one_liner: CDN, DNS, security and edge-compute platform.
records.blocker: None — free plan, scoped API tokens.
records.note: Scoped API tokens preferred over the legacy global key. Cloudflare publishes a whole family of remote MCP servers.

records.one_liner: Postgres-backed backend-as-a-service.
records.blocker: None — generous free tier; Management API uses a personal access token.
records.note: Data API is PostgREST auto-generated from the schema, so the surface differs per project — a real modelling problem for a generic toolkit.

records.one_liner: Graph database with a managed Aura cloud.
records.blocker: None — Aura Free tier; the primary interface is Cypher over Bolt/HTTP rather than a resource REST API.
records.note: Aura management API uses client id/secret; the database itself uses basic auth. Vendor-published MCP servers (Cypher, Aura, memory).

records.one_liner: Cloud data warehouse and AI data platform.
records.blocker: None to trial (30-day credits); production is a paid contract.
records.note: OAuth, key-pair JWT, programmatic access tokens, and workload identity federation. Snowflake-managed MCP server serves Cortex Analyst/Search/Agents as tools.

records.one_liner: Managed MongoDB with an admin control-plane API.
records.blocker: None — M0 free cluster; Admin API keys use HTTP Digest, service accounts use OAuth2.
records.note: Digest auth is unusual enough that a generic OAuth/API-key toolkit model will get it wrong by default.

records.one_liner: Observability: metrics, logs, traces, monitors.
records.blocker: None to trial; note the two-key model.
records.note: Writes need an API key; reads need API key AND application key. Multi-site (US/EU/AP/Gov) base URLs must be configurable.

records.one_liner: Error monitoring and performance tracing.
records.blocker: None — free tier, org auth tokens.
records.note: Auth tokens with space-separated scopes; OAuth2 authorization code for third-party apps; legacy API keys disabled for new accounts.

records.one_liner: Docs, wiki and database workspace.
records.blocker: None — free plan; every page must be explicitly shared with the integration, which is the real friction.
records.note: Internal connection tokens, user-scoped PATs, or OAuth 2.0 public connections.

records.one_liner: Spreadsheet-database hybrid for operational data.
records.blocker: None — free plan; legacy API keys were deprecated on 1 Feb 2024, so PAT/OAuth only.
records.note: Official server at mcp.airtable.com ships 12 tools across bases, tables, records, fields.

records.one_liner: Issue tracking for software teams.
records.blocker: None — free plan and personal API keys.
records.note: GraphQL-only. Remote MCP at mcp.linear.app.

records.one_liner: Atlassian issue tracking and project management.
records.blocker: None — free tier up to 10 users; basic auth uses email + API token.
records.note: Docs recommend OAuth 2.0 3LO over basic auth for anything beyond scripts.

records.one_liner: Work management and task tracking.
records.blocker: None — free tier and PATs.
records.note: The authentication-quick-start URL 404'd during research; the MCP doc resolved and confirms the platform. Row kept at medium confidence for that reason.

records.one_liner: Visual work OS for teams.
records.blocker: None — free plan; API call budgets vary by plan.
records.note: 'Personal tokens mirror all permission levels set in the monday.com UI.' GraphQL-only.

records.one_liner: All-in-one project management app.
records.blocker: None — free plan, personal tokens that 'never expire'.
records.note: Personal tokens (pk_) that "never expire", or OAuth 2.0. Official remote MCP at mcp.clickup.com, public beta on every plan — found only because the 404 probe page carried 36 MCP mentions.

records.one_liner: Docs-as-apps workspace with tables and automations.
records.blocker: Ownership churn: coda.io/developers now 307-redirects to docs.superhuman.com, so doc URLs and long-term API stability are in flux.
records.note: Bearer API token. The redirect was discovered by the agent, not anticipated — a good example of retrieval catching a corporate change.

records.one_liner: Spreadsheet-style work and project management for enterprise.
records.blocker: API access is a paid-plan feature; trials work for development.
records.note: Bearer access token or OAuth2. Smartsheet MCP server reached GA in 2026.

records.one_liner: Time tracking and invoicing.
records.blocker: None — 30-day trial and a free single-user tier; PATs are the documented preference.
records.note: 'Personal Access Tokens are the preferred method when you want to write your own scripts that consume our API.' Requires Harvest-Account-Id header.

records.one_liner: Payments, billing and financial infrastructure.
records.blocker: None — test-mode keys work immediately; live mode needs business onboarding.
records.note: HTTP Basic with the secret key as username. Restricted keys (rk_live_) for least privilege. Stripe also ships agent skills and a CLI 'stripe agent setup' — the most agent-ready vendor in the set.

records.one_liner: Bank account connectivity and financial data.
records.blocker: Sandbox is instant and free, but Production access requires an application/approval and a commercial agreement. 'Items cannot be moved between environments.'
records.note: client_id + secret in the request body or PLAID-CLIENT-ID / PLAID-SECRET headers — no bearer token.

records.one_liner: Crypto exchange with spot/futures trading APIs.
records.blocker: Keys are self-serve after KYC, but jurisdictional restrictions (notably the US) and request signing make this a compliance question as much as an engineering one.
records.note: HMAC, RSA or Ed25519 signatures plus timestamp/recvWindow on SIGNED requests; REST + WebSocket.

records.one_liner: NMI-powered payment gateway front-end (merchant-facing).
records.blocker: No public developer documentation found under this name. The underlying NMI gateway does publish public docs, so any toolkit would target NMI's Payment API with merchant-issued credentials.
records.note: Honest gap: three searches and two fetches produced nothing branded 'Paygent Connect'. Recorded as unresolved rather than invented — the single lowest-confidence row in the dataset.

records.one_liner: FX forensic audit layer that scores cross-border payment spreads.
records.blocker: None — mid-market rates work with no key at all; a free key unlocks live provider comparison.
records.note: MCP-native: the product ships as an MCP server (mcp.ipayx.ai/mcp) with four tools before it ships as a conventional API. Baseline pass had this as 'gated, unknown'.

records.one_liner: Intuit's SMB accounting platform.
records.blocker: None to develop — free sandbox company; production apps go through Intuit review before publishing.
records.note: Fetch of the auth page was truncated by page size; classification rests on the developer portal structure. Marked medium rather than high for that reason. Probe confirmed a vendor MCP docs page on developer.intuit.com.

records.one_liner: Cloud accounting for small business.
records.blocker: None to develop — free developer account and demo company; public apps need certification.
records.note: OAuth2 with PKCE; machine-to-machine 'custom connections' are a paid add-on. Vendor MCP server published under the XeroAPI org.

records.one_liner: Corporate cards and spend management.
records.blocker: You must already be a Brex customer with an account/card admin role, and accept the Developer API agreement. No sandbox for outsiders.
records.note: User tokens via bearer header; OAuth reserved for partners.

records.one_liner: Corporate cards, bill pay and spend management.
records.blocker: Customer-only: OAuth2 client credentials are issued from within a Ramp account; sandbox access is requested, not self-serve.
records.note: A candidate MCP docs path returned a page with no MCP content, so no MCP claim is made.

records.one_liner: Private-market company, deal and investor data.
records.blocker: Paid platform subscription PLUS a separate Direct Data contract, both negotiated with sales. No free tier, no trial, no public endpoint reference, no self-serve signup.
records.note: Correct finding is 'commercially gated', not 'no API'. Existing customers request access via Plugins & Apps in the PitchBook platform.

records.one_liner: Google's source-grounded research and notebook assistant.
records.blocker: No consumer API. The only programmatic path is Gemini Notebook Enterprise (formerly NotebookLM Enterprise/Agentspace) inside Google Cloud, with service-account/OAuth auth and enterprise contracting.
records.note: Enterprise API covers notebook CRUD, sources, audio overviews; developers report no first-class chat/query endpoint for full RAG orchestration.

records.one_liner: Meeting recording, transcription and summaries.
records.blocker: The public REST API and webhooks are Enterprise-only and enabled by an account manager. Ironically the official MCP server (mcp.otter.ai/mcp, live since March 2026) works on every plan including free Basic.
records.note: The clearest case in the set of MCP arriving before the API — a toolkit here means proxying MCP, not REST.

records.one_liner: AI meeting notetaker with CRM sync.
records.blocker: None — API access is included on all plans including free; CRM match data requires the Business plan.
records.note: REST at api.fathom.ai/external/v1 with TypeScript/Python SDKs, webhooks, OAuth2 for public integrations, plus an MCP server.

records.one_liner: AI search over 200M+ peer-reviewed papers.
records.blocker: MCP is self-serve (mcp.consensus.app/mcp, OAuth, no account needed to start); the raw enterprise API is bearer-token and sales-gated.
records.note: Name collision hazard: goconsensus.com is an unrelated demo-automation vendor whose API is Enterprise-plan-only. The first search conflated the two — a human had to disambiguate.

records.one_liner: Document parsing and extraction for AI pipelines.
records.blocker: None — free tier; enterprise is contact-sales.
records.note: Six capabilities (classify, parse, extract, split, edit, pipelines), 30+ file types, Python/Node/Go SDKs, plus an MCP server.

records.one_liner: Cognition's autonomous software-engineering agent.
records.blocker: Paid Devin subscription.
records.note: Service-user credentials ('cog_' prefix) for RBAC or personal access tokens. Organization + Enterprise API scopes: sessions, knowledge, playbooks, secrets.

records.one_liner: AI video/image generation suite for creators.
records.blocker: API is gated behind higher-tier plans and documentation is thin; pricing and plan names have changed repeatedly.
records.note: Cloud API at cloud.higgsfield.ai with an official higgsfield-client Python SDK. Mostly third-party evidence — flagged low confidence.

records.one_liner: CLI that renders Mermaid diagram text to SVG/PNG/PDF.
records.blocker: Not a SaaS API — an npm package (@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli) that shells out to headless Chromium. A toolkit means running it, which means sandboxing and a browser dependency.
records.note: Belongs in the 'local tool / agent skill' bucket rather than the 'connected app' bucket.

records.one_liner: transcriptapi.com — YouTube transcript and metadata API.
records.blocker: None — 100 free credits with no card, paid plans from ~$4.50/mo.
records.note: Bearer API key. Endpoints for transcripts, search, channels, playlists, plus a published 'YouTube MCP'.

records.one_liner: Meeting recording, notes and coaching for revenue teams.
records.blocker: Paid plan for the API; tokens are generated in workspace settings.
records.note: Three auth modes including Personal Access Tokens ('same level of access as the user that generated the token'). Requires a Public-Api-Version header (2025-10-31); 300 requests/min per token. developers.grain.com blocked automated fetches (403) — resolved via the support-site mirror.
